text:
elaine (Docs): Quick sweep please — I just opened the draft release notes for 0.9.7-gamma: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321. Main asks: tighten feature bullets, confirm known-issues wording, and sanity-check the new SDK streaming-embed snippet.

mike r: On it. Which snippet are you most worried about? the JS streaming example or the Go embed client?

elaine (Docs): JS streaming one looks fragile due to response shape changes from the model. Also we added a migration note for customers moving from /embeds to /embed-streaming — need wording that doesn't scare non-technical PMs.

jasmin: I can take the migration note. Suggest: short TL;DR + one example showing old -> new HTTP flow. Keep it <3 lines, then link to the detailed migration guide.

samir: I pulled the PR. SDK snippet in docs/examples/embed-stream.md uses this block:```js
const resp = await client.embeddings.stream({ model: "rwd-embed-lite", input: ["a", "b"] });
for await (const chunk of resp) {
  // handle chunk
}
```
We changed the server to emit an initial metadata object now, so example needs to show a metadata check or skip. If not updated, users will be confused.

olivia: Good catch. Suggest small edit: add comment about metadata header and show `for await (const chunk of resp) { if (chunk.type === 'meta') continue; }`

mike r: I'll push a commit to the PR with that exact snippet. Also noticed one of the feature bullets says "batch caching reduces per-token costs by up to 4x" — we should change to "can reduce" and link to the benchmark doc. Legal asked for less absolute claims.

elaine (Docs): Agreed. Replace with: "can reduce per-token costs in latency-tolerant workloads; see benchmark link." Add the benchmark link to the inline parentheses.

docs-bot: PR 4321 updated: +3 commits, reviewers requested: jasmin, mike r.

jasmin: For the known-issues section — there's an entry "embed-streaming may drop first token under heavy load". Is that still accurate?

samir: We fixed a race last week; edge case remains only for models with input length > 64k and extremely high-concurrency. Rename it to: "Edge-case: very long inputs (>64k) with peak concurrency may exhibit missing early tokens; workaround: enable prefix-caching or upgrade runtime."

elaine (Docs): Perfect. Also we have a small UX copy tweak for the What's New blurb — internal PM wants less jargon. Current: "introduces prefix/KV caching and quantization-friendly kernels." Change to: "introduces smarter request caching and model optimizations to lower cost and latency."

olivia: I'll make that copy change in the top-level blurb and add an internal note: (PM-approved).

mike r: Two more micro things I noticed: 1) a broken link in the changelog anchor — /docs/api#embeddings -> should be /docs/api/embeddings. 2) the Go SDK snippet uses `client.Embeds(...)` old method name — needs rename to `client.Embeddings.Create(...)`

elaine (Docs): Please include the exact fix in your commit messages so the relnotes pipeline picks them up (e.g., "fix: replace broken embeddings anchor" and "fix: go sdk method rename").

jasmin: I'll draft the 3-line migration TL;DR now and paste it here for quick approval: "If you're calling /embeds, switch to /embed-streaming for live streaming results. Most clients will only need a one-line change to the request path; see the migration guide for code examples and a compatibility table."

elaine (Docs): That sounds good — two tiny edits: change "one-line" -> "small" and add a note: "No model changes required."

jasmin: Edited: "If you're calling /embeds, switch to /embed-streaming for live streaming results. Most clients will only need a small change to the request path; no model changes required. See the migration guide for code examples and a compatibility table."

samir: For the compatibility table: I'll export the current matrix from the internal service and drop it into the migration guide as a CSV link. Heads-up: it shows some older quantized variants won't stream. I'll add a short note in the guide.

olivia: I'm going to run linkcheck locally against the PR branch. If anything else is broken I'll post fixes here.

docs-bot: linkcheck: running on pr/4321...

mike r: Uploaded the snippet fixes and the doc copy changes to the branch. PR now includes: snippet metadata handling, go rename, anchor fix, blurb rewrite.

docs-bot: linkcheck: completed. 2 broken links found.

olivia: Found them: 1) internal benchmark link pointing to private S3 (should be replaced with public benchmark doc), 2) old redirect for /docs/api/embeddings that still 301s. I'll fix both and push.

elaine (Docs): Amazing — after those two fixes, can we aim to merge by EOD? I want release notes published with the platform patch tomorrow morning.

jasmin: I'm happy to approve once the migration TL;DR and compatibility CSV link are in.

samir: CSV link uploaded to the PR as artifacts/compat-matrix.csv.

docs-bot: PR 4321: reviewers approved: jasmin, mike r. Ready to merge.

mike r: Merged. :tada:

elaine (Docs): Thanks team! I'll schedule the release-note publish job for 08:00 UTC tomorrow. Small follow-up: please monitor the docs relnotes page after publish for any formatting glitches (bullet indentation often trips the renderer).

olivia: Will watch and fix if needed.

mike r: FYI - I'll open a tiny follow-up PR to add a rendered snippet screenshot to the JS example so readers know what to expect.

elaine (Docs): Sounds good. Closing loop: action items summarized — jasmin: migration TL;DR (done), mike r: snippet + go rename (done), olivia: link fixes + linkcheck (done), samir: compat CSV (done). I'll post the release publish job ID in #release-war-room once scheduled.

samir: Nice flow. Great job all.

elaine (Docs): :heart:
